title: Put Marbles in Bags
statement:
You are given an array `weights` of `n` marbles in a row and an integer `k`. You must split the row into exactly `k` non-empty **contiguous** parts (bags): every marble goes into exactly one bag, and each bag holds a consecutive block of marbles.

The cost of a bag that holds marbles `i` through `j` (inclusive) is `weights[i] + weights[j]`: the weight of its first marble plus the weight of its last marble. A bag with a single marble costs twice that marble's weight. The **total cost** of a split is the sum of the costs of its `k` bags.

Across all possible ways to split the row into `k` bags, find the maximum total cost and the minimum total cost, and return **maximum minus minimum**.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers `weights[0] ... weights[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum total cost minus the minimum total cost.

examples.explanation: There are three splits: `[1] [3 5 10]` costs 2 + 13 = 15, `[1 3] [5 10]` costs 4 + 15 = 19, and `[1 3 5] [10]` costs 6 + 20 = 26. The difference between the largest (26) and smallest (15) is 11.

The first and last marbles always contribute fixed amounts. Each cut between marbles `i` and `i+1` adds `weights[i] + weights[i+1]`. The four possible cuts add 9, 8, 9, 11; the best two cuts add 11 + 9 = 20 and the worst two add 8 + 9 = 17, so the answer is 3.
With one bag there is only one split, so the maximum and minimum are equal.

hints: Write the total cost of a split in terms of its cuts. The very first marble and the very last marble are always bag endpoints, so they contribute the same amount in every split.

Each cut between positions i and i+1 ends one bag at i and starts the next at i+1, so it adds exactly weights[i] + weights[i+1]. A split with k bags uses k - 1 cuts, and any set of k - 1 distinct cut positions is allowed.
So the maximum picks the k - 1 largest adjacent-pair sums and the minimum picks the k - 1 smallest. Sort the pair sums and subtract.
